title: Copy and Move for Owning Types
summary: A class that owns memory must decide what copying and moving mean. The rule of five, a deep copy, a move that steals the pointer and leaves the source empty, copy-and-swap for safe assignment, self-assignment, and the rule of zero - letting members that already own do it all.

cards.q: What goes wrong when a class owning a raw new[] array uses the default copy constructor?
cards.a: Both objects hold the same pointer, so both destructors delete the same array.

cards.q: What must a move constructor do to the object it moved from?
cards.a: Leave it valid but empty, typically setting its pointer to nullptr, so its destructor frees nothing.

cards.q: Why should a move constructor be noexcept?
cards.a: std::vector only moves elements when growing if the move cannot throw; otherwise it copies them.

cards.q: What is the rule of zero?
cards.a: If every member manages its own resource, the class needs no destructor and no copy or move functions of its own.
